title: MT5 Gold EA Results, Long-Only Strategy with AI Trade Filtering
author: CommandantZ
selftext:
Hey everyone,

I wanted to share the results of my MT5 Expert Advisor and discuss possible improvements to the strategy. A bit of background first: I've been developing EAs for about 7 years now, both professionally and for myself. 

The EA trades Gold (XAUUSD). It can also trade Forex pairs, but the strategy discussed here is specifically designed for Gold.

The concept is simple: the EA only opens long positions, based on Gold's long-term bullish bias. Most trades are scalps and are closed quickly for small profits.

**The main challenge is avoiding periods where Gold enters a bearish phase**. To handle this, I use an AI model, not for generating entries, but as a trade filter. The model analyzes market structure and looks for potential reversals (Break of Structure / market regime changes). When such a signal is detected, the EA stops opening new positions.

The AI is also used for trade management. Most positions are opened with a predefined Take Profit, but occasionally the AI decides not to set one, suggesting a higher probability of continued upside. These "standalone" trades are then managed manually.

I've attached screenshots from MyFXBook and MT5, including an example of a standalone trade. You'll also notice a few small drawdowns on the equity curve; these were mostly caused by my own manual trades rather than the EA itself.

comments.author: YouMatter202
comments.body: I have a strategy but don’t know where to start.How did you start? If you can please tell.

replies.author: CommandantZ
replies.body:
First things first, you need to make sure your strategy is something that can be automated. When I develop bots for clients, I often get instructions such as "when I see that blablabla", but "seeing" is not something I can just code within a bot. So you need to have precise instructions, as in:

if blabla happens, then execute blabla, with blabla.

Then, I suggest you can either hire a freelancer to code it for you, or code it yourself (maybe helped by AI, typically Claude does okay, not perfect but okay) and I generally suggest MQL5, as the layer of abstraction it provides is great.

I personally had a manual trading strategy that I automated, and then from there kept backtesting, launching it live, then revamping and so on.

replies.author: CommandantZ
replies.body:
I'll be honest it depends a lot on the strategy you are implementing and as well from where do you get your freelancer. But you can expect anything between 100 USD to 1000 USD. You may find them on MQL5 Freelance or Upwork.

Some are very cheap, but be wary of the code quality.

replies.author: lucaxplayer_
replies.body:
Buongiorno, se hai bisogno potremmo parlare.  
Ormai non uso più le piattaforme di freelancer perché le persone ti fanno più perdere tempo che altro .  
Io ho realizzato le mie strategie trasformandole su Python e poi su mql5 , e chiaramente associato a una buona qualità di dati TICK backtest ho potuto migliorarle al fine di renderle più stabili e durature nel tempo.  
Tuttavia grazie ai backtest sono riuscito anche a capire ( su certi bot , chiaramente non su tutti ) e affinare le fasce di orario dove funzionava bene la mia strategia e “oscurare” le ore dove perdeva soldi per via delle aperture e chiusure di mercato o news pesanti .

Ad ogni modo tutto ad oggi è possibile programmare , serve solo organizzazione e tempo . Chiaramente su richiesta di potrebbe creare , per chi odia star dietro a valori nudi , una Dashboard comoda

replies.author: lucaxplayer_
replies.body:
Good morning, we could talk if you need help.  
I no longer use freelance platforms because people waste my time more than anything else.  
I created my strategies by converting them to Python and then to MQL5, and obviously, combined with good-quality TICK data and backtesting, I was able to improve them to make them more stable and long-lasting.  
However, thanks to backtesting, I was also able to understand (on certain bots, obviously not all) and refine the time slots where my strategy worked well and "black out" the times when it lost money due to market openings and closings or heavy news.

In any case, everything is programmable these days; it just takes organization and time. Of course, upon request, a convenient dashboard could be created for those who hate keeping track of raw values.
